s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated epididymal involvement and adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
No response to 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology
Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis
No uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation
Negative serologies for active HCV and EBV
Positive for past EBV

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and epididymal involvement

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and associated epididymal involvement

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement and testicular pathology

shortlist.label: Testicular plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and absence of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painless testicular swelling and the ultrasound findings of testicular enlargement and inhomogeneity, along with the intense uptake on 18 FDG PET/CT, are consistent with a testicular tumor. The absence of systemic symptoms and the lack of uptake in the adrenal glands make metastatic disease less likely. Leydig cell tumors are known to cause testicular enlargement and can present with hormonal effects, but this patient's normal laboratory evaluation does not show evidence of hormonal imbalance. However, Leydig cell tumors are more likely to present with localized disease as seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and rapid progression, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with testicular swelling and may have elevated LDH or beta-hCG, but this patient's laboratory evaluation is normal.

rejected.label: Adrenal metastasis from testicular cancer
rejected.why: The adrenal nodules are new and bilateral, but the 18 FDG PET/CT showed no uptake in the adrenal glands, making metastasis less likely.

rejected.label: Testicular plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Typically associated with multiple myeloma, but this patient's laboratory evaluation, including protein electrophoresis, is normal, making this diagnosis unlikely.
